The study has specified the safety factor – the Nadal criterion – against the derailment of the wheels of a railway stock. Unlike in the traditional approach, the safety factor of the wheel steadiness against derailment is assessed taking the frame force, rather than the lateral load on the flange, as the main factor of safety. This approach to determining the stability criterion gives more reliable results, since the frame force is more accessible for experimental and theoretical analysis.

research_gaps: Limited ML/AI application to derailment probability prediction
Insufficient digital twin models for real-time track monitoring
Limited sensor-fusion approaches for early derailment warning
Sparse research on derailment risk in mixed-speed traffic corridors
Emerging need for autonomous inspection system validation frameworks
key_findings: Wheel-rail contact mechanics significantly influence train derailments, with research focusing on contact forces, wheel climb, and derailment dynamics
Advanced testing and simulation methods have improved understanding and safety
Derailments cause financial and environmental damage
Railway engineering focuses on track geometry irregularities to prevent derailments, using spectral analysis and derailment coefficient assessments for safety
Peer-reviewed research emphasizes the importance of track condition and dynamic risk modeling for derailment prevention
AI-driven models enhance track defect rectification and risk assessment
Derailment probability modeling uses statistical analysis to estimate risks based on train length, speed, and track conditions
Peer-reviewed research shows that track class, operation method, and traffic density significantly affect derailment rates
Improved track modeling enhances safety and maintenance efficiency
High-speed rail dynamics simulation studies focus on derailment safety, analyzing wheel-rail interactions and curve negotiation abilities
